Mallary CLI

Mallary CLI is the official command-line interface for the Mallary public API.

Purpose
- Upload local media to Mallary storage/CDN infrastructure. This transmits selected local file bytes
- Create and schedule social posts
- Inspect jobs and grouped posts
- List comments and reply to comments on published posts
- Fetch analytics
- Manage webhooks
- Read and update brand/settings data
- List connected platforms
- Disconnect connected platforms

Install
- npm install -g @mallary/cli
- npx @mallary/cli --help

Authentication
- Interactive default: browser-based OAuth with `mallary auth login`
- OAuth grants read, publish, engage, and manage access in one login; users do not choose scopes
- A clear user request to publish, schedule, upload media for that post, or send a reply authorizes that action; do not ask for a second confirmation
- Ask only when a material detail is missing or ambiguous, and do not widen the request
- Check the active method without exposing credentials: `mallary auth status`
- Optional CI/advanced override: MALLARY_API_KEY
- When MALLARY_API_KEY is set, it takes precedence over stored OAuth
- Authentication alone is not a request for a state-changing command; a clear user request is the authorization boundary
- Most CLI commands require a paid Mallary plan: Starter, Pro, or Business

Base URL behavior
- Base URL is fixed: https://mallary.ai
- Health uses /health
- Authenticated commands call /api/v1/*

Command inventory
- mallary health
- mallary upload <file...>
- mallary posts create
- mallary posts list
- mallary posts delete <id> (destructive: deletes queued/scheduled Mallary post/job that has not started publishing)
- mallary comments list --post-id <id>
- mallary comments reply --post-id <id> --comment-id <cid> --message "text"
- mallary jobs get <id>
- mallary analytics list
- mallary audience list
- mallary webhooks list
- mallary webhooks create
- mallary webhooks delete <id>
- mallary settings get
- mallary settings update --file partial.json
- mallary platforms list
- mallary platforms disconnect <platform> (destructive/account-impacting: disconnects a platform until reconnect)

Output conventions
- Human-readable output by default
- Use --json for automation
- Direct API wrapper commands emit the API response body in --json mode
- Convenience flows emit CLI-shaped JSON:
  - upload returns { ok, uploads }
  - posts create returns { ok, uploads, response } when local files were uploaded first

Typical workflows
1) Upload media:
   mallary upload ./image.png --json
2) Create post from flags:
   mallary posts create --message "Hello" --platform youtube --media ./video.mp4 --thumbnail ./cover.jpg --json
   Use --post-type when every selected destination should use the same supported type.
3) Create post from a raw JSON payload:
   mallary posts create --file ./post.json --json
4) Poll a job:
   mallary jobs get 123 --json
5) List grouped posts:
   mallary posts list --json
6) Engage with comments:
   mallary comments list --post-id 123 --json
   mallary comments reply --post-id 123 --comment-id "1789..." --message "Thanks for checking this out."

Important constraints
- The CLI is a direct client for the public API. It does not bypass plan limits or validation rules.
- Free-plan users can use `comments list` and `comments reply`. Other CLI commands return `upgrade_required`.
- Settings updates are file-based in v1.
- Flag mode supports one shared explicit format through --post-type.
- For advanced per-platform payloads or different types by destination, prefer posts create --file.
- comments_under_post remains limited by the API.
- Media must be local files uploaded through Mallary or already-hosted `https://files.mallary.ai/...` URLs.
- Video thumbnails use `media[].thumbnail_url` in JSON file mode, or `--thumbnail` with exactly one `--media` item in flag mode.
- Thumbnail URLs must be local files uploaded through Mallary or already-hosted `https://files.mallary.ai/...` URLs.
- External third-party media URLs are rejected by the CLI.

Platform-specific payloads
- Use `--post-type` in flag mode when each selected platform should use the same supported type.
- Use `platform_options` in file mode for other platform-specific fields or different types by destination.
- Use `platform_options.<platform>.message` for platform-specific messages/captions.
- Supported examples:
  - facebook: `message`, `post_type` (`feed`, `story`, or `reel`), `link`, `pageId`
  - instagram: `message`, `post_type`
  - linkedin: `message`, `author_urn`
  - youtube: `message`, `post_type`, `title`, `visibility`, `categoryId`, `madeForKids`
  - tiktok: `message`, `post_type`, `post_mode`, `source`, `title`, `description`, `privacy_level`
  - pinterest: `message`, `post_type`, `boardId`, `link`, `alt_text`
  - reddit: `message`, `post_type`, `subreddit` or `subredditName`
  - threads: `message`, `post_type`
  - x/twitter: `message`
  - bluesky: `message`, `languages` or `langs`; media items can use `alt_text`

Format discovery
- `mallary platforms list` is read-only and returns each destination's selectable `post_types`.
- Preserve an explicitly requested Story, Reel, Short, carousel, photo, or video.
- Never silently replace a requested format with a feed post or another type.
- If a destination does not list the requested type, stop and report the mismatch.

Post enhancements
- `comments_under_post` supports up to 3 follow-up comments.
- Mallary supports custom video thumbnails/covers for YouTube regular videos, Facebook videos, and Instagram videos/Reels. TikTok video posts do not accept arbitrary image thumbnails through Mallary. TikTok photo posts can use `thumbnail_url`. It works only when the URL matches one of the supplied photo URLs.
- `auto_reply_enabled` can be set per post, but AI auto-replies still require an eligible paid plan plus a complete brand profile in settings.

Out of scope
- OAuth connect flows
- Dashboard onboarding endpoints
- Admin/observability endpoints
- MCP transport/client behavior
